# dtcloud_security_group_rule (Resource)

Manages one rule inside a security group.

The API has a create endpoint and a delete endpoint and nothing else, so the whole resource forces replacement. That is exactly what the platform does anyway -- delete the old rule, create the new one -- and the plan says so.

The resource ID is `<security-group-id>:<rule-id>`: a rule is read by listing its group's rules, and a bare rule id cannot say which group to list.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Allow SSH from one address range.
resource "dtcloud_security_group_rule" "ssh_from_office" {
  security_group_id = dtcloud_security_group.web.id
  direction         = "ingress"
  protocol          = "tcp"
  port_range_min    = 22
  port_range_max    = 22
  remote_ip_prefix  = "10.10.0.0/16"
}

# Allow traffic from every machine in another group. Referring to a group rather
# than to an address keeps the rule correct as machines come and go.
resource "dtcloud_security_group_rule" "app_from_web" {
  security_group_id = dtcloud_security_group.app.id
  direction         = "ingress"
  protocol          = "tcp"
  port_range_min    = 8080
  port_range_max    = 8080
  remote_group_id   = dtcloud_security_group.web.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `direction` (String) Traffic direction: `ingress` (inbound) or `egress` (outbound).
- `security_group_id` (String) ID of the security group this rule belongs to.

### Optional

- `ethertype` (String) Address family: `IPv4` or `IPv6`. Defaults to whatever the platform picks, which is `IPv4`.
- `port_range_max` (Number) Last port in the range. For `icmp` this is the ICMP **code**, not a port. Omit for all ports.
- `port_range_min` (Number) First port in the range. For `icmp` this is the ICMP **type**, not a port. Omit for all ports. See the note on 0 below.
- `protocol` (String) Protocol the rule matches, e.g. `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, or a protocol number. Omit it to match every protocol. Not restricted to a fixed list, because the platform accepts more than the common names.
- `remote_group_id` (String) ID of another security group whose members the rule applies to. An **id**, not a name — the platform does not resolve names here. Mutually exclusive with `remote_ip_prefix`.
- `remote_ip_prefix` (String) CIDR the rule applies to, e.g. `10.0.0.0/24`. Mutually exclusive with `remote_group_id`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `description` (String) Description of the rule. Read-only: the create route does not accept one, so this is only ever non-empty for a rule created outside Terraform.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `normalized_cidr` (String) `remote_ip_prefix` with its host bits cleared, as the platform computes it — `10.0.0.5/24` is reported here as `10.0.0.0/24`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# A rule is found by listing its group, so the import id carries both ids:
# <security-group-id>:<rule-id>
terraform import dtcloud_security_group_rule.ssh_from_office 7f9c1e40-1c3d-4b6a-9a2f-5f1c9d0e3b11:2b8d5a71-90ce-4f2a-8d13-6c0b4e7a1f22
```
